transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

Hello. Well, mostly I'm here because I just don't sleep right anymore. I go to bed and... I just lie there a long time. Then when I do finally drop off, I end up waking up from bad dreams or even just little noises, and I can't seem to settle back down after that.
Are the bad dreams the main reason you wake up at night?

The dreams are a big part of it, yeah. But it's not just the nights that are the problem. Even during the day, sometimes when I hear metal scrape, or... or if I just see a ladder leaning up in somebody's yard, the whole thing jumps right back in my head. It's like I'm right back under there again, just waiting for help.
How long ago did the event under the ladder happen?
Well, let's see... it was about a year and seven months ago. This has all been going on ever since that accident happened.
Since the accident, have you been avoiding things that remind you of it, such as ladders, construction areas, or conversations about what happened?

Well, yes, I suppose I have been. I just... I keep finding reasons not to go out to the garage anymore. That's where I used to keep the ladder, and all my tools are out there. I just don't want to be around them. And I've been staying away from the senior center, too, because they've been doing some work on the roof there, and... well, I just don't want to see it or talk about it.
Since the accident, have you felt more on guard or watchful than you were before?

Yes, I guess I have. When I go places now, I... well, I look around a lot more than I used to. I check to see if there's anything that might fall on me. I look for where the exits are, just in case. And I always make sure the floor or the steps look steady before I can finally sit down and feel easy. I just can't seem to relax until I've checked everything out.
Since the accident, have you felt emotionally detached or unable to feel close to other people?

Yes, I have. It's hard to explain, but... well, my wife will be sitting right there next to me, or the fellows from my bridge group will be joking around, and I just feel... disconnected. Like I'm behind a glass window or something, watching them but not really with them. It's just a strange feeling of being apart from everyone.
Are your bad dreams about the ladder accident?

Well, yes, they are. But mostly... well, mostly I'm here because I just don't sleep right anymore at all. I'll lay there a long time at night before I finally drift off, and then I wake up from those bad dreams, or even just from little noises in the house, and... well, I just can't seem to settle back down after that.
On nights when you do not have a dream about the accident, do you still have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep?

Yeah, like I was just saying... it's really not just the dreams. Even on a night where I don't have one, I still just lie there staring at the ceiling for a long time. And if I do finally drop off, just a little creak or noise in the house is enough to wake me right back up. Once my eyes are open, dream or no dream, I just can't seem to settle back down to sleep.
How much do your sleep problems interfere with your functioning during the day?

Well, I still manage my basic routines, getting up and dressed and all that. But... I guess it takes a toll. I've stopped going down to the senior center, for one. And I avoid enough things around the house now that my wife has had to take over chores I used to always handle. I just don't have it in me. I don't visit with my bridge friends much anymore, either. It just feels like my days have gotten a lot smaller.
Do you have enough time and a suitable environment to sleep, yet still have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep?

Yes, I've got plenty of time. I'm retired, so there's no rush in the mornings, and our bedroom is perfectly fine and quiet. But like I was saying earlier, I just don't sleep right anymore regardless of all that. 

The room is fine, but I still just lie there awake for a long time. And then when I do wake up in the middle of the night—whether it's from those bad dreams or just some little noise in the house—I just can't seem to settle back down to save my life.
Are your bad dreams always about the ladder accident, or do you also have distressing dreams about unrelated topics?
They're just about the accident. I don't really have bad dreams about anything else, just... just falling off that ladder.
